newsitem.title: USA: Eleven New York jail guards accused of beatings.
newsitem.headline: Eleven New York jail guards accused of beatings.

text.p: Eleven New York City jail guards were accused Wednesday of beating up inmates and covering up the violence by filing false reports about the incidents, officials said.
The 11 suspects, one of whom now works as a New York City police officer, used "excessive force" against three inmates at the city's Rikers Island jail, according to the indictments.
They allegedly punched and kicked one inmate, dragging him from his cell and causing him multiple head and body injuries, the indictments said.

In another incident, an inmate bound in handcuffs and leg-irons was struck in the face and stomach while he was being escorted to a clinic for medical attention following a fight with another inmate, the indictments said. The inmate required more than two dozen stitches to close up his wounds, they said.
The indictments were unsealed Wednesday after an investigation of more than two years.

"These were planned, deliberate beatings and were unprovoked by the inmates," said Robert Johnson, district attorney in the city's Bronx borough. "These indictments should send a clear message that no one is above the law. It applies to everyone."

Johnson said evidence against the 11 defendants includes secretly made tape recordings, admissions by some defendants and testimony of confidential informants. "We are not relying on what the inmate alleges occurred," he said.
The defendants pleaded not guilty at arraignments before Bronx Supreme Court Judge Steven Barrett.

The U.S. Attorney in Manhattan filed federal charges against two of the corrections officers recently, alleging they violated the civil rights of jail inmates. That case is scheduled to go to trial at the end of this month.
